newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures slip again late,end near lows.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures slip again late,end near lows.

text.p: IMM currency futures slipped again in late pit trading, with most ending moderately to sharply lower and hugging pit-session lows.
Futures pulled back again during the final hour as the dollar returned above 124.00 yen, or about $0.008100 in March yen futures, although brokers said they saw no big futures sellers on the move.
"It was a cash move back above 124 yen," said one floor broker. "That's what pushed it."
About the same time, U.S. Treasury bond futures pared losses and stocks expanded gains, adding currency pressure.
March marks had popped up briefly to the pit-session peak as T-bond futures eroded to the day's low following a 10-year Treasury note sale that drew less demand than expected.
The 10-year note sold at an average yield of 6.374 percent, with a two-basis-point tail, a 1.90 bid/cover ratio and $424 million in non-competitive bids.
Traders had expected a 6.37-38 percent average yield and a higher bid/cover.
"It (10-year sale) was a little disappointing," said the floor broker. "It started off like a roof-shaker and then it just died."
During the quick bounce upward, March marks hit small buystops near $0.5960 that carried the contract to the day's peak at $0.5970 but lacked upward extension on spotty volume.
They said sentiment was unchanged from a few days ago, with many seeing more currency downside but at a slower pace.
"Everything's intact. There's really nothing new to say," added another floor broker. "Rubin's (U.S. Treasury secretary Robert Rubin) said we want a strong dollar about 57 times."
He said his firm expected any rise in the dollar above 1.6950 marks to open the door for a test of the 1.70 mark level, or roughly $0.5895 in March mark futures.

Overnight, March marks had hit a new contract low before comments from Bundesbank pared losses. A Bundesbank spokesman said the German central bank sees "no substance" in a report Tuesday by Market News Service that said sources close to the German finance ministry and Bundesbank said Germany would welcome a dollar rise to 1.70-1.75 marks over time.

March yen ended down $0.000072 at $0.008092, marks lost $0.0032 to $0.5948, Swiss francs fell $0.0066 to $0.6923, sterling fell $0.0030 to $1.6324, Can dollar fell $0.0013 to $0.7387, Aussie dollar rose $0.0020 to $0.7591, Mexican peso rose $0.000225 to $0.126575.
